content: A thread I wrote on Bluesky about how the RSS world, an earlier instance of the writer's web, was overtaken by Twitter and why, which boils down to this -- the reading platforms wouldn't work with each other. So Twitter made subscription one click. And RSS made sites include 25 buttons to give people one-click subscription in every feed reader with users. Twitter only needed one button. And it worked every freaking time. Now, 18 years later, the twitter-like systems world, Mastodon, Threads, Substack, Ghost, Bluesky mostly can't get together on a simple way to peer. They keep talking about it and while they do, we're losing everything that's important to us. We have gotten ruined as a democracy because we trusted Silicon Valley to handle our politics. In the open tech world we have the same problem as the Democratic Party. We refuse to see how the world has changed, and our slow and steady approach leads nowhere fast. I don't know what we need to win, but I do know what we need to get started. Maybe it's not too late? What else have we got to do but try.
